advice: Proposal: fuse A transposition with GEMM tile consumption. Base: `existing-sme`, SHA-256 `3719c58530161598ab9a537a43be749a5287c8d8dbd35b855e5afea97cd15258`. Do not write those A values to the full `at` scratch in this path. Keep B access, FP32 arithmetic, MOPA selectors 0–3, increasing-k order, and the general-size fallback unchanged. This removes full-matrix transpose scratch traffic, but repeats tile loading/transposition for each output-column tile: 16 repetitions for n=512. Hypothesis: saved scratch writes and reads may offset repeated transpose work; measure the whole timed `gemm` call, including allocation and all data movement.
risks: This is unverified. Repeated A tile loads and ZA-to-SVE extraction may cost more than the removed scratch traffic. Fusing may also increase live state or spills, and ZA tile read semantics and edge handling need full-path validation. Do not claim a gain or infer its cause from noisy scores.
